Subject: Spike + intermittent 503s during Black Friday peak (logs attached)

Hi Priya —

We saw a pattern of increased tail latency and intermittent 503s on 2028-11-25 between 19:12 and 20:03 PST that materially impacted our checkout flow during Black Friday. Impact summary: ~12% checkout failures for a 30-minute window and elevated p99 token latency for the 90 minutes after.

We need: 1) confirmation of a service disruption/downtime window that would meet Redwood's SLA definitions, 2) list of raw traces and any evaluated root cause indicators, and 3) whether ParcelWorks is eligible for a credit under our contract (deal PW-4392). I've attached a small sample of client-side traces and a screenshot of the checkout error.

Attachments: raw_traces_blackfriday_20281125.log.gz (sample), checkout_503_screenshot.png

Please escalate as needed — this was a high-revenue period for us.

Thanks,
Asha Patel

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 Nov 2028 10:18:05 -08:00
Subject: RE: Spike + intermittent 503s during Black Friday peak (logs attached)

Priya / David —

I've pulled the matching server-side traces and correlating router metrics for 2028-11-25. Preliminary findings:
- A congestion event in the US-west routing plane caused request queueing increase starting 2028-11-25T19:08:22-08:00, with a visible spike in 5xx responses between 19:12:47 and 19:47:58 PST (approx 35 minutes).
- P99 token generation latency increased from baseline ~120ms to ~2.1s during the peak window; p95 stayed near 430ms.
- The root trigger appears to be an autoscaler mis-evaluation combined with a simultaneous model cache warm-up on a small percentage of the serving fleet; two warmups correlated with brief KV cache evictions for long-context models.

I’ve attached a server-side trace bundle (full bundle saved to our internal case) and included a small excerpt below.

Excerpt (server trace):
[2028-11-25T19:12:49.223Z] req=0x7f4c... queued=312ms backend_latency=1840ms status=503 route=us-west-2/model-bert-large seq_len=120
[2028-11-25T19:20:11.011Z] req=0x8a3b... queued=28ms backend_latency=2100ms status=200 route=us-west-2/model-bert-large seq_len=256

I recommend we: 1) confirm the official downtime window as 2028-11-25T19:12:47 - 2028-11-25T19:47:58 PST for entitlement math (35m), 2) bundle the full traces and checksums for audit, and 3) schedule a postmortem with ParcelWorks and our infra team.

I will push the full log bundle to the case and share a secure link.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 29 Nov 2028 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Spike + intermittent 503s during Black Friday peak (logs attached)

Hi Asha —

Thank you for your patience while we ran the telemetry and correlated server traces. Per Karthik’s analysis, Redwood is confirming a service-impact window that we believe meets the SLA availability definition for a partial outage. We propose the following:

Confirmed impact window (for SLA): 2028-11-25T19:12:47 PST — 2028-11-25T19:47:58 PST (35 minutes)
Evidence provided: server trace bundle (full), excerpt sent, client traces you uploaded, and router metric dashboards.
Preliminary credit calculation: Because the confirmed window exceeds the SLA downtime threshold for PW-4392 and per Section 4.2 of your contract, we propose a pro-rata credit equal to 2.1% of monthly committed usage for November 2028 (calculation: 35min / month-available-time adjusted by purchase tier). I’ve attached a spreadsheet with the line items (credit_calculation_proposal.xlsx).

Next steps:
- Please confirm receipt of the server trace bundle (attached as raw_traces_blackfriday_20281125.log.gz) and the proposed credit worksheet.
- We’d like to schedule a 30-minute postmortem review the week of Dec 4 to walk through root cause, mitigation, and any contractual questions. Tentative link: https://cal.com/redwood/postmortem-30min
- If you have alternate impact numbers (e.g., your 12% metric measured differently), please share them and we’ll reconcile.

If ParcelWorks confirms the calculation we’ll turn the credit into a formal account adjustment within five business days and publish a short postmortem summarizing corrective actions (autoscaler tuning and cache-warmup order changes).

Apologies again for the disruption — we know timing was awful and we’ll prioritize follow-through.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
